clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Statutory Pay Systems. Pursuant to the Continuing Appropriations 
and Surface Transportation Extensions Act, 2011 (H.R. 3082), which I signed 
into law today (the ‘‘Continuing Appropriations Act ’’), the rates of basic 
pay or salaries of the statutory pay systems (as defined in 5 U.S.C. 5302(1)) 
are set forth on the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: (a) The General Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5332(a)) at Schedule 1;

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: (b) The Foreign Service Schedule (22 U.S.C. 3963) at Schedule 2; and

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) The schedules for the Veterans Health Administration of the Department 
of Veterans Affairs (38 U.S.C. 7306, 7404; section 301(a) of Public Law 
102–40) at Schedule 3.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Senior Executive Service. The ranges of rates of basic pay for senior 
executives in the Senior Executive Service, as established pursuant to 5 
U.S.C. 5382, are set forth on Schedule 4 attached hereto and made a part 
hereof.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Certain Executive, Legislative, and Judicial Salaries. The rates of 
basic pay or salaries for the following offices and positions are set forth 
on the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: (a) The Executive Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5312–5318) at Schedule 5;

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and the Congress (2 U.S.C. 31) 
at Schedule 6; and

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Justices and judges (28 U.S.C. 5, 44(d), 135, 252, and 461(a), and 
section 140 of Public Law 97–92) at Schedule 7.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. Uniformed Services. The rates of monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 
203(a)) for members of the uniformed services, as adjusted under 37 U.S.C. 
1009, and the rate of monthly cadet or midshipman pay (37 U.S.C. 203(c)) 
are set forth on Schedule 8 attached hereto and made a part hereof.

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text:
Sec. 5. Locality-Based Comparability Payments. (a) Pursuant to section 5304 
of title 5, United States Code, the Non-Foreign Area Retirement Equity 
Assurance Act of 2009 (Public Law 111–84; 5 U.S.C. 5304 note), and the 
Continuing Appropriations Act, locality-based comparability payments shall 
be paid in accordance with Schedule 9 attached hereto and made a part 
hereof.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take such 
actions as may be necessary to implement these payments and to publish 
appropriate notice of such payments in the Federal Register.

clauses.label: Sec. 6.
clauses.text:
Sec. 6. Administrative Law Judges. Pursuant to section 5372 of title 5, 
United States Code, the rates of basic pay for administrative law judges 
are set forth on Schedule 10 attached hereto and made a part hereof.

Executive Order 13561 of December 22, 2010 
Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the laws cited herein, 
it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Statutory Pay Systems. Pursuant to the Continuing Appropriations 
and Surface Transportation Extensions Act, 2011 (H.R. 3082), which I signed 
into law today (the ‘‘Continuing Appropriations Act ’’), the rates of basic 
pay or salaries of the statutory pay systems (as defined in 5 U.S.C. 5302(1)) 
are set forth on the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof: 
(a) The General Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5332(a)) at Schedule 1; 
(b) The Foreign Service Schedule (22 U.S.C. 3963) at Schedule 2; and 
(c) The schedules for the Veterans Health Administration of the Department 
of Veterans Affairs (38 U.S.C. 7306, 7404; section 301(a) of Public Law 
102–40) at Schedule 3. 
Sec. 2. Senior Executive Service. The ranges of rates of basic pay for senior 
executives in the Senior Executive Service, as established pursuant to 5 
U.S.C. 5382, are set forth on Schedule 4 attached hereto and made a part 
hereof. 
Sec. 3. Certain Executive, Legislative, and Judicial Salaries. The rates of 
basic pay or salaries for the following offices and positions are set forth 
on the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof: 
(a) The Executive Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5312–5318) at Schedule 5; 
(b) The Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and the Congress (2 U.S.C. 31) 
at Schedule 6; and 
(c) Justices and judges (28 U.S.C. 5, 44(d), 135, 252, and 461(a), and 
section 140 of Public Law 97–92) at Schedule 7. 
Sec. 4. Uniformed Services. The rates of monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 
203(a)) for members of the uniformed services, as adjusted under 37 U.S.C. 
1009, and the rate of monthly cadet or midshipman pay (37 U.S.C. 203(c)) 
are set forth on Schedule 8 attached hereto and made a part hereof. 
Sec. 5. Locality-Based Comparability Payments. (a) Pursuant to section 5304 
of title 5, United States Code, the Non-Foreign Area Retirement Equity 
Assurance Act of 2009 (Public Law 111–84; 5 U.S.C. 5304 note), and the 
Continuing Appropriations Act, locality-based comparability payments shall 
be paid in accordance with Schedule 9 attached hereto and made a part 
hereof. 
(b) The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take such 
actions as may be necessary to implement these payments and to publish 
appropriate notice of such payments in the Federal Register. 
Sec. 6. Administrative Law Judges. Pursuant to section 5372 of title 5, 
United States Code, the rates of basic pay for administrative law judges 
are set forth on Schedule 10 attached hereto and made a part hereof.

defects.source_says: EO 13594 (76 FR 80191) is dated December 19, 2011, and its section 8 states 'Executive Order 13561 of December 22, 2010, is superseded.' The date 2008-12-19 is two years before EO 13561 itself was signed (December 22, 2010), and it contradicts the claim's own judgment_reason and research_rationale, which give 2011-12-19.

defects.claim_says: section 8 ('Executive Order 13525 of December 23, 2009, is superseded') ends by EO 13594's supersession
defects.source_says: Section 8 is a self-executing supersession of EO 13525, performed when EO 13561 took effect on 2010-12-22. Under the method the project applies to other revocation clauses, its first end is that performance date, which is earlier. The earlier-end test was not applied to this clause. The whole-order end is unaffected.

cruden.py number search of held order texts, written to /tmp/claude-0/review-o23-EO_N.json
record.reasoning: Identity (75 FR 81817, signed 2010-12-22), the 15-clause inventory, the quotations and the identification of EO 13594 section 8 as the ending instrument are correct, and cruden confirms that no earlier held instrument names EO 13561. The disclosed note about EO 13594 section 7's January 1, 2012 schedule dates is reasonable. However, every recorded end date is 2008-12-19, which predates the order and contradicts both the source and the claim's own reasons. Reject.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 13561 sets pay rates for the statutory pay systems, the Senior Executive Service, executive, legislative and judicial salaries, uniformed services, locality payments and administrative law judges by attached schedules, and in its last section supersedes its predecessor. Section 8 of the later Executive Order 13594 says that Executive Order 13561 'is superseded' without a qualifying effective-date clause, and the later order was signed on 2011-12-19. That express supersession of the whole order is recorded as the first end of every clause. The later order's section 7 gives its own schedules effective dates, and for the Schedule 8 and other schedules those dates may precede the signing date; this is disclosed as a note for the reviewer. A search of held order texts for the number 13561 finds the later order, and the later order is the earliest held instrument naming this one.
